title: API compatibility, stability lifecycle, and migration playbook
author: Priya Raman
content:
Summary

This playbook defines Redwood’s recommended approach for API compatibility, stability guarantees, and structured migration/deprecation for platform services. It is intended for service owners, platform engineers, SDK/consumer owners, release managers, and customer-facing engineering teams. Follow this lifecycle to minimize customer disruption, keep dashboards actionable, and ensure predictable rollouts.

Scope

- Applies to all public and internal HTTP/JSON APIs, streaming endpoints, gRPC services, and client SDK interfaces exposed by the platform.
- Excludes ephemeral operator CLI flags used for deploy-time debugging (see appendix).

Goals

1. Keep breaking changes explicit and rare.
2. Provide clear versioning and migration paths.
3. Ensure monitoring + alerts surface compatibility regressions quickly.
4. Standardize communication and support SLAs for migrations and deprecations.

Ownership and roles

- Service Owner: accountable for change design, rollout plan, and documentation.
- SDK/Client Owner: updates SDKs, publishes migration guides, coordinates consumer compatibility tests.
- Platform Release Manager: approves staged rollouts and tracks signoffs.
- Observability / SRE: publishes dashboards and configures SLI/SLOs and alerts.
- Customer Success: crafts customer comms for top-tier accounts when applicable.

Stability Tiers (how we classify endpoints)

- Tier 0 (Stable): Public, production-facing endpoints with SLA. No breaking changes without full version bump and 90-day migration period.
- Tier 1 (Guarded): Internal production endpoints used by multiple teams. Breaking changes allowed with 30–60 day migration window and automated feature flags.
- Tier 2 (Experimental): New features or alpha endpoints. Can be removed or changed with 7–14 days notice.

Versioning scheme

- Semantic major versioning is required for public contract changes. Major version changes must be implemented as vN in URI or as an independent API surface (e.g., /v2/predict or X-API-Version: 2).
- Minor/patch: additive, backward compatible changes. Use X-API-Compat: minor=+ header when returning new fields to callers that opt-in.

Compatibility matrix (example)

| Change type | Allowed in-tier | Required action | Minimum notice |
|-------------|----------------|-----------------|----------------|
| Add field to response | Tier 0/1/2 | Document and include opt-in header for strict clients | immediate |
| Remove response field | Tier 0 | Major version bump or alias + 90 days | 90 days |
| Change field type | Tier 0/1 | Major version bump or new field + deprecation | 60–90 days |
| Remove endpoint | Tier 0 | New version + migration guide + traffic split | 90 days |
| Change URL path | Tier 1/2 | Redirect + compatibility shim | 30 days |

Migration lifecycle: recommended procedure

1. Design: write a short design doc describing the change, compatibility impact, acceptance tests, migration plan, monitoring targets, and rollback criteria. Attach to the PR.
2. Approval: obtain signoff from Platform Release Manager and Observability/SRE if change affects SLAs.
3. Implementation: implement both new and old behaviors behind a feature flag or versioned endpoint. Provide server-side shim where feasible.
4. Smoke tests: run end-to-end compatibility test suite against staging and canary. Include SDK consumers in the loop.
5. Canary rollout: 1% / 10% / 50% / 100% progression with health gates (see rollout gates below). Each step should be at least 30 minutes of steady metrics for high-traffic services.
6. Communication: publish migration guide, changelog, and targeted emails for major customers 30/14/7/1 days before hard deprecations.
7. Deprecation enforcement: after the grace period, redirect traffic to the new endpoint and monitor errors for 72 hours. If error rate exceeds threshold, rollback and open a mitigation runbook.

Rollout gates and metrics (SRE guardrails)

- Successful gate requires:
  - Latency p95 within +15% of baseline for new version,
  - Error rate (4xx/5xx) less than 0.1% absolute increase or 3x baseline relative increase (whichever is smaller),
  - Token cost per request (+/-) within expectation for LLM inference endpoints.
- Gate check artifacts: canary telemetry snapshot, end-to-end consumer test pass, and release manager approval.

Alerting and dashboards

Recommended dashboards to create whenever an API change is staged:
- Compatibility healthboard: 5m/1h/24h error trends grouped by API version and consumer app.
- Contract drift alerts: monitors for unexpected schema changes (unexpected keys/types) detected by ingest pipeline.
- SDK consumer error spikes: top-10 consumer apps by error increase.
- Migration progress: % traffic by version, number of consumers migrated, and open issues.

Alerting thresholds (examples)
- Contract drift: any schema mismatch > 0.5% of requests over 10m -> pager to service owner.
- Canary latency degradation: p95 increase >15% sustained for 10m -> page SRE and service owner.
- Consumer failure storm: >50 distinct client error spikes in 30m -> page oncall + Customer Success for affected tier-1 customers.

Runbook: compatibility incident (high level)

1. Triage: identify impacted API versions and consumers. Use the Compatibility Healthboard and logs to find the earliest failing commit.
2. Rollback check: determine if rollback to previous implementation is faster than hotfix. If canary was used, revert the canary and re-route traffic.
3. Hotfix: if regression path is small and testable, apply hotfix behind feature flag and canary again.
4. Communication: post incident status on internal incident channel and update customer-facing status page if consumer-visible.
5. Post-incident: open RCA with action items and update migration playbook sections if needed.

Deprecation timeline template (Tier 0)

| Phase | Duration | Activity |
|-------|----------|----------|
| Announcement | Day 0 | Publish deprecation notice + migration guide + target owners list |
| Soft deprecation | Day 30 | Log warnings in responses (Warning header: API-Deprecation) and surface in dashboards |
| Hard deprecation | Day 90 | Redirect or remove endpoint; begin errors after last redirect window |
| Sunset | Day 120 | Remove deprecated codepaths from runtime and SDKs after final audit |

Communication checklist

- Internal: Jira ticket, release PR, Slack channel, and link to design doc.
- External (public): roadmap update, changelog entry, SDK release notes.
- Tiered customer comms: targeted emails to customers who used the deprecated endpoint (identified via telemetry) with migration steps and contact for support.

Testing and compatibility automation

- Maintain a compatibility test harness repository: include contract tests (schema checks), feature tests, performance budgets.
- Add consumer smoke tests: owners must add at least 1 end-to-end test that runs in the platform CI for Tier 0/1 changes.
- Use CI gating: changes that modify API schema must fail CI when they break contract tests.

SDK and client guidance (examples)

- Opt-in fields: prefer returning new fields with an opt-in request header X-API-Compat: feature=name so strict clients are not broken.
- Version header example:
  curl -H "X-API-Version: 2" https://api.redwood.ai/v2/predict

- Example deprecation warning header:
  Warning: 299 - "API v1 deprecated; see /docs/migrate-v1"

Retrospective cadence and success metrics

- After each major migration or deprecation, hold a 60-minute retrospective within two weeks.
- Measure: number of impacted consumers, mean time to rollback, number of post-cutover incidents, customer satisfaction score for migration.

Appendices

A. Migration checklist (copyable)
- Link design doc to PR.
- Create migration guide in /docs.
- Add SLI/SLO targets to canary dashboard.
- Configure alerts and runbooks.
- Notify SDK owners and top-10 consumers.
- Schedule retrospective.

B. Example contract test (pseudo-YAML)
  - request: POST /v1/predict
    body: {"input": "test"}
    assertions:
      - response.status == 200
      - response.schema.contains("predictions")

C. Quick rollback CLI snippets
  - # revert canary weight to 0%
    curl -X POST https://platform-api/internal/rollout -d '{"service":"predictor","weight":0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${PLATFORM_OPS_TOKEN}'

Related resources

- API Standards doc: /confluence/eng-platform/api-standards/
- Observability onboarding: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/platform-observability-sli-onboarding-playbook-2026

Notes and exceptions

- For security-sensitive changes (auth, encryption), the deprecation window may be shorter; consult Security & Compliance and include a restricted migration plan.
- Breaking changes required by external compliance can be fast-tracked by the Platform Release Manager with customer success coordination.
